key_insight: Generalized Feynman-Kac correctors enable principled sampling from arbitrary functions of multiple pretrained diffusion models, including reward-steered targets, without retraining.
engineering_relevance: The framework lets practitioners compose and steer existing diffusion models while correcting sampling errors introduced by naive score combination.
method: Derive a Feynman-Kac PDE and closed-form potential for geometric interpolation from an initial function to the target.
Generalize the log-probability ODE to track each model’s density along trajectories driven by a different velocity field.
Apply corrections during generation entirely in the log domain, with optional reward-based steering.
evidence_signal: Tests on analytic Gaussian models closely match ground-truth targets, while MNIST experiments demonstrate non-trivial model combinations and effective steering.
watch_item: Evidence in the abstract is limited to Gaussian and MNIST settings; scalability and computational overhead for larger models remain unclear.
paper_title: Composing and Steering Diffusion Models with Generalized Feynman-Kac Correctors
